title: The rule package registry and the workbook object are declared in the P3 module and owned by P7
source: Legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 3, 4, 11, 12 and 13 (rule_package_version writes, the Blob workbook, RulePackageEffectiveDateJob); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T2.1 (RulePackageRepository) and T3.1 (rule_package and rule_package_version 'owned by P4'); Ownership Map v1 (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case, owner P7, ruling ASM-A6-tables-3); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 27 and 41; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15
section: s2 Business rationale; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story loads, approves, promotes and rolls back a package version and writes rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case, the generated DRL and the workbook Blob object from inside the case module, and its preconditions require a job_catalog row for RulePackageEffectiveDateJob. The ownership ruling and Architecture v5 put the four registry tables, the model registry, the workbook object, the five authoring operations and the 00:01 promotion in rwb-decision, which leaves rwb-case with the evaluated copy, the case fact mapping, the version pin, the scenario gate and a consumed contract only. Three of the fifteen legacy criteria therefore name an artefact this service does not own: the rule_package_version.checksum and Blob metadata of AC15, the rule_package_version row and Blob object of AC13, and the promotion wording behind AC1 and AC4. This story proves those against the rwb-decision contract mock and carries the registry work to RWB-P7-E1073-APP, with the real cross-service proof in RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-073 section 13: 'The load writes rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case in one transaction'; section 11: DF-REF-279 to DF-REF-294 are written by this story; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 headings 'rule_package (NEW, owned by P4)', 'rule_package_version (NEW, owned by P4)', 'rule_test_case (NEW, owned by P4)'; Ownership Map v1 owner P7 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-3 'services hold only a local evaluated copy (DP-04)'; Architecture v5 slide 41 P7 'approvals, central decision ledger, DMN model registry'; Temporal and Drools slide 15 'governance ... is central in rwb-decision (P7)'
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-073 (AC1, AC4, AC13, AC15; sections 3, 4, 11, 12 and 13)
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the P3 tech lead
proposed: Keep the registry, the workbook object, the five authoring operations, the approval, the promotion Schedule JOB-20 and the rollback in RWB-P7-E1073-APP under ASM-A6-tables-3; keep the case fact mapping, the version pin, the scenario gate and the consumed contract in RWB-P3-E1073-APP and RWB-P3-E1073-CON; correct the TSD P3 v3 ownership labels for the four tables; prove the registry statements against the rwb-decision contract mock here and against the real service in RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG.

title: The five authoring operations and the two rule reads have no Ownership Map row and no field-level shape
source: Ownership Map v1 api section (P3 and P7 rows); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (P7 IN: POST /rule-models, GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}); legacy RWB-E1-073 section 12 (the five admin paths on the monolith base); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T2.2 (RuleResult, RuleCatalog.row)
section: s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Build steps
description: RWB-P3-E1073-CON and RWB-P3-E1073-APP consume seven operations of rwb-decision: the load, the version list, the approve, the rollback, the dry run, the model read and the catalog read. The Ownership Map lists no row for any of them, Architecture v5 slide 14 names only POST /rule-models and GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} and the legacy section 12 gives the five admin paths on the retired monolith base with no owner in the target. The rollback and dry-run answer shapes, the catalog element names and the property types of both reads are therefore assumed here. This key fixes the element names, the rights, the answers, the error codes and the fakes on Day 1 and leaves the types to the review with the rwb-decision owner.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 api rows for P7 list GET /cases/{caseId}/recommendation, GET /approvals, the three approval actions, GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} and no rule-package or rule-model row; Architecture v5 slide 14 P7 IN: 'REST GET /decisions?caseId= ... POST /rule-models, GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}'; legacy RWB-E1-073 section 12 paths under the monolith base; TSD P3 v3 T2.2 gives the Java signatures RuleResult and RuleRow but no wire shape
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the solution architect
proposed: Add the seven operations to the P7 rows of the Ownership Map and to the rwb-decision API file with their rights, answers and error codes, and publish the model and catalog resources with packageCode, versionLabel, checksum, valid-from date, compiler version, ruleId, action_text, owner_role, timer_spec, target_queue_code and outputs; until then the RWB-P3-E1073-CON baseline and its WireMock fakes carry the assumed shapes and paths.

title: The KieBase cache sizing, the JVM heap and the storage of a local model artefact are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-073 preconditions ('rules.testcases.min = 50 (assumed)' and 'drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20') and section 13; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 27 (evaluation under 300 ms, cache, checksum); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16 (KieBaseRegistry, LRU, max 20)
section: s11 Data; s13 Solution plan; s17 Guardrails; s19 Out of scope (RWB-P3-E1073-INF)
description: No source states the heap a pod of rwb-case needs to hold the KieBase cache of at most 20 package versions plus the working set of the service, and no source says whether a compiled model may be written to a local volume or is rebuilt in memory after a restart. The legacy story names the cache bound and the test count as parameters, marks the test count assumed and gives no deployment figure at all. RWB-P3-E1073-INF exposes the heap, the cache bound and the model life cycle as reviewed values per environment, proves them with a load test that holds the cache bound and evaluates under load, and records them as assumptions rather than as business values.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-073 precondition: 'rules.testcases.min = 50 (assumed) and drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20 are in the catalog'; Architecture v5 slide 27: 'Load GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, verify checksum, swap in' and 'Evaluate Inside an activity, under 300 ms'; Temporal and Drools slide 16: 'KieBaseRegistry holds one KieBase per package version (LRU, max 20), never recompiled per call', with no memory figure and no storage statement
owner_role: SCB IT infrastructure with the rwb-case owner team
proposed: Size the pod by a load test that holds the cache bound of 20 package versions and evaluates under load, record the heap request, the heap limit and the cache bound per environment as reviewed values, keep the evaluated copy in memory only, and confirm the values with the platform owner before the wave 1 release.

title: No source gives the readiness gate, the probe timings, the ports, the certificate subject or the image-scan window
source: Legacy RWB-E1-073 preconditions (the rwb-decision dependency and the module identity); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20 and 27 (mTLS, one namespace, the model in force); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T2.5 (temporal.target, mTLS certificates from the ACE internal CA, the worker identity)
section: s11 Data; s13 Solution plan; s14 Validation and messages; s19 Out of scope (RWB-P3-E1073-INF)
description: The deployment story must decide when a pod is ready, with which probe timings, on which ports, with which certificate subject and with which image-scan window and patch cadence. No source gives any of them: the legacy story names no deployment value, Architecture v5 gives the mechanism of mTLS and the model in force but no threshold, and TSD P3 v3 gives the parameter names without values. RWB-P3-E1073-INF therefore exposes every one of them as a reviewed value per environment under one assumption, so the operator sees a pod without a model in force before a case reaches it without the story inventing a business value.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-073 precondition: 'the rwb-decision front end presents a certificate the platform certificate authority issued' equivalent wording and no port or timing; Architecture v5 slide 11 and slide 20 give mTLS and the namespace shape only; TSD P3 v3 T2.5: 'temporal.target | Frontend gRPC address per environment | Internal only; port 7233' with no probe, readiness, scan or certificate-subject value; no threshold appears in FSD P3 v4 or the Drools design
owner_role: SCB IT infrastructure with the platform administrator
proposed: Record the readiness gate, the probe timings, the ports, the certificate subject and the image-scan window as reviewed values per environment in the deployment files, confirm them with the platform and security owners at SIT, and keep every one of them out of code and out of a chart constant.
